Meeting Number-34
Today's meeting commenced at 13:25 hrs under the chairmanship of the Rt. Hon'ble Chairperson of the National Assembly, Mr. Narayan Prasad Dahal.
(13:24 hrs)
Chairperson: - Honorable Members of the National Assembly, the proceedings of today's meeting will now commence. Honorable Members, I have allocated a maximum of 4 minutes for speaking during the "Special Time". I will now provide time to the honorable members sequentially. First, Honorable Member Anand Prasad Dugana.
(Nepali Congress):- Honorable Mr. Anand Prasad
(13:26 hrs)
- Respected Chairperson, a situation has arisen in the country where shots are being fired, from Sunsari to Madhesh. We had believed that the Home Minister would provide some information about the incident today after the session commenced. However, the Home Minister is not present. As far as we have learned, it's not authorized information, but as far as we have learned, you have held a seven-point discussion in Sunsari. But we do not know what that seven-point discussion was about. Therefore, I want to say that the kind of ethnic conflict, we have various ethnicities, languages, and cultures living together in this country. Nepal is a multi-ethnic, multi-lingual country. In the current situation where incidents are occurring in this country, the Prime Minister of Nepal, or rather the Prime Minister, needs to take personal interest and move forward with this work. Yesterday, you removed a weed. A statement is not enough for the Nepali people. The Nepali people have died. What is the cause of their death? The police fired shots, used force. Perhaps the situation could have been resolved by reasoning with them, but instead, shots were fired using force, and you are responsible for it. I want to tell the government that the government should find an immediate solution. Furthermore, after that, the fire spread, and the government's whereabouts were unknown for four days. The incident in Sunsari reached Siraha. Ganesh Yadav in Golbazaar, Siraha, and Ganesh Yadav in Tulsipur also died yesterday. The government says it doesn't know who fired the shots. Now, what I find strange is that they fire shots themselves and then say they will investigate who fired the shots. Shots were fired haphazardly like this. Not only that, Mr. Chairperson, Suvas Thakur from Ward No. 8 of Dhanusha Dham Municipality in my constituency was also shot. Two people were shot; where did the shots come from, who fired them? The entire market in Golbazaar has been set on fire. This situation is escalating in the country. It happened in Siraha and Dhanusha. After that, Gaushala Bazaar and Jaleshwar Bazaar in Mahottari are also closed. Similarly, in Sarlahi, they are announcing to gather at Ram Mandir. A prohibitory order has been issued in Parsa. In this way, all districts of Madhesh are affected, and in Supari, the court proceedings were closed yesterday due to a curfew. This shows that the government has been asleep while fires are spreading across the country, leading to ethnic conflict. The Prime Minister has been sought by honorable members for four months in the House of Representatives, asking him to come and respond, to clarify what he said. There are reports that Nepalis have had their land seized in India; how true is this? What the Prime Minister said might be true in the House, but I want to say that the Prime Minister, who tries to make false things true, why did the Prime Minister not attend the all-party meeting called by the Rastriya Swatantra Party President the other day? We, the leaders of each party, were present at the all-party meeting; they might have had their experiences. They have struggled for 70 years in this country, and today we have achieved a federal democratic republic, we have achieved this constitution. If this constitution is lost, if this country becomes weak, if democracy becomes weak, where will the Nepali people go? Today, I have seen in many places that many countries have been broken and destroyed due to the weakening of your country and democracy. Some elements are trying to create that situation. Therefore, I want to say that if the Home Minister had dealt with this communal conflict that has arisen in time, he reached there yesterday, four days later, by airplane... (Time expired).

Honorable Chairperson: - Honorable Member Jayanti Devi Rai.
(13:31 hrs)
Honorable Ms. Jayanti Devi Rai (Nepali Communist Party):- Respected
(13:31 hrs)
Chairperson, on the 11th of Saun, Sunday evening, in Devanaganj Rural Municipality Ward No. 3 of Sunsari district, a dispute arose over a DJ music system and religious flags during a Bolbam procession, which led to a clash. This clash has affected Sunsari and some districts of Madhesh Province. The daily life there is disrupted, there is a curfew, and vandalism and arson are occurring. Three people have died, and several have been injured, including security personnel. I express my sorrow over this tragic incident and offer my heartfelt condolences to the deceased and wish a speedy recovery to the injured, and I also demand that the government make necessary arrangements for their treatment and provide due compensation to the families of the deceased.
Today, Respected Chairperson, looking at the nature of this incident, it is becoming more complex, and today this incident is escalating internal conflict and war, and it is promoting social harmony and religious tolerance. Therefore, I want to say that the government does not seem to be taking this extremely sensitive incident seriously. Even when an all-party meeting is called, the Prime Minister should have spoken himself, taken action himself, but he was not present at the all-party meeting. In the four days, he only addressed it yesterday, perhaps if he had addressed it immediately after the incident occurred, such damage might not have happened.
Therefore, I want to tell the government today that it must first answer why the shots were fired today? Under whose orders? And were they really fired by the police or by someone else? The truth must be revealed, and an investigation must be conducted. Today, people have died. Why are the security agencies and mechanisms becoming weak and controversial today? Therefore, I want to tell the Respected Chairperson today that the Prime Minister should be summoned to this parliament to answer these questions. It is not possible to resolve the problem by just writing a status update on such a sensitive incident. Therefore, to prevent human loss from this incident and to mitigate it, I want to draw the serious attention of the government to take immediate steps. I also humbly and heartily request all parties from this House to maintain peace, stability, social harmony, mutual unity, and religious tolerance. Thank you.

Honorable Chairperson: - Honorable Member Roshi Mechhe.
(13:35 hrs)
Honorable Mr. Roshi Mechhe (Nepal Communist Party, UML):- Respected
(13:34 hrs)
Chairperson, through this esteemed House today, I want to draw the serious attention of the parliament and the government to the extremely sensitive and unprecedented violent incident that occurred in Devanaganj, Sunsari. The killing of local youths Om Prakash and Jaiprakash Mehta by firing in Kapilanaganj, and similarly, the state's cruel and barbaric act that took the life of Ganesh Yadav in Siraha, has shocked and saddened me. I offer my condolences to the deceased and express my deep sympathy to the bereaved families.
Protecting the life and property of citizens and resolving problems through dialogue to lead the country towards peace is the primary responsibility of the government. However, I strongly condemn the indifference shown by the government and the excessive use of force even when national security and social order have reached a sensitive stage. Did the government go to save citizens or to fire shots? Mr. Chairperson, while Sunsari and Madhesh Province are burning, the government is trying to prioritize its own agenda by calling an all-party meeting without understanding the gravity of the situation. I want to emphasize this.
While the government should have taken the initiative to resolve the problem by calling an all-party meeting, the fact that the chairperson of the ruling party itself had to call an emergency all-party meeting, and the Prime Minister and Home Minister were absent from that meeting, is it silence in crisis or arrogance? During a crisis, we need a Prime Minister who stands in parliament and answers, not a leader who hides behind video messages. Mere video messages and hollow words of sympathy cannot wash away the blood of innocent citizens. The stain of this blood will not be erased by video sympathy. Mr. Chairperson, it is completely unacceptable to divert the main issue by blaming the media, ethnic communities, police, and local government to hide one's own failures. This dual inhumane character is never acceptable.
Mr. Chairperson, this incident is not merely an accidental local lapse; it has not even been a week since the IGP himself testified before a parliamentary committee about the growing communal challenges in Madhesh. Despite that, this extreme negligence and irresponsibility of the state is an unforgivable and serious security failure, but the government is trying to hide its moral and leadership incompetence by calling it merely religious and communal, which is extremely shameful and condemnable. If the leadership is held responsible when shots are fired in Kathmandu, can the police administration be blamed when shots are fired in Sunsari? In a democratic governance system, the ultimate responsibility for security failure always lies with the political leadership. When police fired shots during the Bhadra movement, did the Balen government, which imprisoned the then Prime Minister and Home Minister, forget its own actions today?
Mr. Chairperson, I want to call upon this House that we have all built this nation together, comprising all ethnicities and communities. The nation and nationality cannot be strengthened through conflict and violence. We cannot move towards resolving problems. Therefore, at a time when national stability, peace, security, and social harmony are under threat, I earnestly appeal to all political parties, civil society, intellectuals, and various social and religious leaders to unite for the sake of national interest and peace. Furthermore, I demand that a high-level judicial inquiry into the Sunsari incident be conducted immediately, that justice and appropriate compensation be provided to the victims' families without delay, and that the Prime Minister and Home Minister take full moral and political responsibility for this nationwide security failure. Thank you.

Honorable Chairperson: - Honorable Member Puja Chaudhary.
(13:43 hrs)
Honorable Ms. Puja Chaudhary (People's Socialist Party, Nepal):-
(13:43 hrs)
Respected Chairperson, today Madhesh is crying, it is burning. But those who are burning Madhesh do not know that we Hindus, Muslims, Sikhs, Christians, Buddhists, we are all one. Our country is a common garden for all. In a democratic system, guaranteeing the security of citizens' lives is also our collective responsibility. Our brotherhood will not be erased in our country, Nepal.

Our country is multilingual, multi-religious, multicultural, and as long as we are here, we have respected and will continue to respect each other's attire, language, and religion. Furthermore, in any situation, we have learned to respect each other with restraint and patience. However, I appeal to everyone through the honorable Speaker regarding the violence and communal tensions that started in Devanaganj, Sunsari and are occurring in various districts of Madhesh Province, to remain restrained, maintain peace and order, and not fall for the spread of misinformation and corrupt ideas. I sincerely appeal to all mothers, fathers, brothers, and sisters. I also express deep sorrow for the damage caused by this violence, communal tensions, and damage to public property. I offer heartfelt condolences to the deceased and wish for the speedy recovery of the injured. I also express heartfelt sympathy to the families of the victims. With the belief that we will move forward by strengthening social harmony, national unity, and mutual brotherhood, I once again humbly appeal through the honorable Speaker to maintain peace and harmony. Finally, I express the wish that the government will wipe away the tears of Madhesh as soon as possible and humbly request that the accused be apprehended and punished as soon as possible. Thank you. Honorable Speaker: Honorable Member Tul Prasad Bishwakarma. (13:45 hrs) Honorable Mr. Tul Prasad Bishwakarma (Rastriya Janamorcha):- Honorable (13:46 hrs) Speaker, today the eastern Terai is in a state of extreme unrest and fear. Nepal is a multi-ethnic, multilingual, and multi-religious, multicultural country. It is a historical fact that people of all ethnicities, languages, and religions have lived together in a harmonious environment. However, the incident that occurred in Sunsari today is extremely sorrowful and painful. Such incidents are undoubtedly a danger bell for the peace of this country and its people, for the existence and prosperity of the entire country. The incidents that have occurred, starting from Devanaganj, Sunsari, have gradually spread to districts like Siraha, Saptari, Mahottari, etc. The government must immediately bring its activeness to the public and show it to them, and the culprits of these incidents must be brought to legal justice. But today the government is sitting with an expert or a statement. I want to tell the government that it is necessary for the government to pay immediate attention to such incidents. It was reported that more force was used by the administration, pre-administration, and security agencies in the initial days of these incidents. That incident continued to create further crisis, and now messages and clips are coming in about extremely provocative and communal slogans and rallies in the media. Therefore, to bring peace to this, the government must be responsible for this entire incident because the government should have paid attention in time, found out the truth, and brought the criminals to justice. Therefore, I call upon all the citizens of the country to remain restrained and not to participate in such communal incitement, such incitement that fuels ethnic violence, and to cooperate in maintaining peace and order in the country, and I offer heartfelt condolences to the deceased in this tragic incident. Honorable Speaker: The order of speaking during the urgent time ends here. (13:52 hrs) I have allocated 1 minute each for speaking during this time. First, Honorable Member Goma Devi Timalsina. Honorable Member Goma Devi Timalsina. Honorable Member Goma Devi Timalsina. Honorable Member Nar Bahadur Bisht. Honorable Mr. Nar Bahadur Bisht (Nepal Communist Party):- Honorable (13:54 hrs) Speaker, today the country is under attack. Our Home Minister traveled from Sunsari to the central Terai and Madhesh a month ago, and after that, the incidents escalated. Today, three people have been shot dead. The families of the deceased, who signed themselves, he himself went and is still in the midst of the protest. It is unfortunate that the CDO office, where the CDO signs, the Home Minister himself went and signed a seven-point agreement. He himself is escalating the violence. It is like being both the healer and the patient; these violent incidents are a weakness of the government. The statements the government is making are disappointing the people. Writing statements themselves and disappointing people. Firing themselves and then going to provide compensation, salary, the kind of work that has been done is condemnable. Thank you. Honorable Speaker: Honorable Member Narayan Dutt Mishra. (13:56 hrs) Honorable Mr. Narayan Dutt Mishra (Nepali Congress):- Honorable (13:56 hrs) Speaker, the tragic incident has shocked the entire country. I offer heartfelt condolences to the deceased and wish for the speedy recovery of the injured. Our civil society has also been repeatedly... it seems to be recovering now. Now, a great responsibility has fallen on its shoulders. Therefore, it is also necessary to show its active presence in sensitive areas of Madhesh and work, even without foreign funds, to show that our civil society comes forward when the country is in dire need. This is because our all-party meetings and experts, experts... it is seen that religious polarization should not be allowed to increase in the country, and mutual harmony and... it seems that the government should also increase surveillance of citizens living in Nepal who have infiltrated from abroad. Thank you. Honorable Speaker: Honorable Member Bhuwan Bahadur Sunar. (13:57 hrs) Honorable Mr. Bhuwan Bahadur Sunar (Nepal Communist Party):- (13:57 hrs) Honorable Speaker, while the country is burning and youth are being murdered, I apologize to the 6 million Dalit community, and the Ravi Walen government did not prioritize making laws regarding Article 40 of the constitution, a fundamental right. I express my objection to the government's intention to ignore the Dalit community. Thank you. Honorable Speaker: Honorable Member Madan Kumari Shah "Garima". (13:58 hrs) Honorable Ms. Madan Kumari Shah "Garima" (Nepal Communist Party):- (13:58 hrs) Honorable Speaker, regarding discrimination against Dalits, the government apologizes to the Dalit community, but Deepa Nepali, who is on a hunger strike, is neither heard nor seen. If the demands of a citizen who raises their voice against discrimination even after an apology are ignored, then what is the use of that apology? It remains only a formality. True apology must be proven not by words, but by justice and behavior. I draw the serious attention of the government through the honorable Speaker to call Deepa Nepali, who has been on a hunger strike at Maitighar Mandala for 105 days, and address her demands, and I make this demand. Thank you. Honorable Speaker: Honorable Member Yuvraj Sharma. (13:58 hrs) Honorable Mr. Yuvraj Sharma (Nepali Congress):- Honorable Speaker, when a community feels insecure and the majority community... when the minority community feels disrespected. On the other hand, when the state's security agencies, ignoring preventive measures for any incident or untoward event, start giving importance only to the use of force, then the untoward incident that occurred in Kaptanaganj turns into a wildfire. Moreover, the lack of accountability in the government is further evident when the honorable Prime Minister and Home Minister themselves are absent from the all-party meeting held regarding this incident. Through the honorable Speaker, I urge the honorable Prime Minister to understand the adverse psychological impact on the minority and majority communities during his oath-taking ceremony, and in a situation where there is a lack of patience, I also request the Prime Minister not to be too arrogant. Finally, I demand an impartial investigation into the untoward violent incidents that occurred in Sunsari and other places. Thank you. Honorable Speaker: Honorable Member Rajendra Laxmi Gaire. (14:00 hrs) Honorable Ms. Rajendra Laxmi Gaire (Nepal Communist Party):- (14:00 hrs) Honorable Speaker, the seeds of conflict between Hindus and Muslims have been sown in Kaptanaganj, Sunsari. This seed has spread throughout Madhesh Province and can spread throughout the country. We had hoped for a stable government, a two-thirds majority government, thinking no one would die. Now, after people have died and been injured in their homes, distributing money by saying 'I will get you a job, I will take responsibility for you' cannot bring stability to this country. The country cannot be run by sympathy, nor can it find a way out. Therefore, the government should become serious in time, and I draw the serious attention of the government through the honorable Speaker to create an environment where we can live together as we did in the past with our inclusive character, and I request that it be ruled. Honorable Speaker: Honorable Member Suresh Kumar Ale Magar. (14:01 hrs) Honorable Mr. Suresh Kumar Ale Magar (Nepal Communist Party):- (14:01 hrs) Honorable Speaker, while sensitive and serious issues are being discussed in this important meeting of the respected National Assembly, the flickering of lights, is this merely a technical glitch or a political conspiracy by the government? I want to draw the attention of the government to this through the honorable Speaker. Regarding the Sunsari incident, much has already been said, so I do not want to go into detail. I just want to say that this country is a country of diversity. Any kind of extremism, ethnic extremism, religious extremism, regional extremism, all of these are condemnable. They have done their work. Therefore, the government must show seriousness and promptness in this regard. But the unfortunate thing is that while claiming to be an express train, we are experiencing the feeling of being a bullock cart. Therefore, this mere video will not work; the government will have to increase its speed and show promptness. Madhesh is burning, and the Prime Minister is from the Madhesi community. Thank you. Honorable Speaker: Honorable Members, the order of speaking during Zero Hour (14:02 hrs) ends here. Honorable Members, names have been received on a party basis for speaking during the Provincial Concerns time. Now I will provide time for the honorable members to speak. First, Honorable Member Krishna Prasad Sitaula, time 15 minutes. After this, Honorable Member Urmila Aryal. Honorable Mr. Krishna Prasad Sitaula (Nepali Congress):- Honorable (14:03 hrs) Speaker, the issue of provincial concerns is a national concern. Honorable members have already raised issues during Zero Hour and Urgent Time. The Prime Minister made a statement yesterday. We get a sense from his statement that the country is heading towards a serious situation. Therefore, I feel it is necessary to speak a little above and beyond limiting myself to Koshi Province as 'Provincial Concerns'. The issue originates from Devanaganj, Sunsari district. First, I want to offer heartfelt condolences to Jayaprakash Mehta, Omprakash Mehta, and Ganesh Yadav, who died in the violent incidents in Devanaganj, Sunsari, and Siraha district, as announced by the government. May their souls rest in peace, I pray to God, and I express condolences to the bereaved families. To those injured in these violent incidents

I wish everyone a speedy recovery. And many people have suffered huge losses of property, there have been fires, vandalism, looting. The government should talk to everyone, assess the damage, and help them get back on their feet. I want to draw the government's attention to this. Mr. Chairman, in this regard, I want to appeal to everyone, to all the religious communities across the country, to all the ethnic communities, to all people of various cultures and attire. I want to appeal that the definition of religion is not violence at all, not in any way. It is not the root of anything. Religion is a path to protect and elevate existence. It speaks of compassion, empathy, love, and social harmony and unity in society. Everyone may have their own ways, their own religions, their own methods of aligning, their own ways of being attached. But the objective of all is love. Not hatred, not violence, not bloodshed, absolutely not. That is merely a strategy to fulfill one's own selfish interests under the guise of religious communities. Therefore, I especially appeal to everyone involved in religious communities to work together across the country to transform this into social harmony and unity. Issues of social harmony are being raised, and we are also hearing questions. Protests are also taking place on the streets. I want to draw everyone's attention to moving forward with such work. After all, if there is no peace, and people have to live in fear, where does democracy remain? What is democracy without peace? And what is peace without democracy? Democracy without peace is a piece of paper. And what is peace without democracy? It is a silent peace. In dictatorial countries, people remain silent out of fear for a long time. Silent peace where no one can raise their voice, express their beliefs. We don't need that kind of peace either. We have brought a vibrant peace and democracy, a democratic system of governance, a system where people can live according to their own beliefs and rights, and move forward based on those beliefs. There is a long struggle in this, I don't need to elaborate. Everyone here knows that, all brothers and sisters across the country know that. The country of Nepal has reached a federal democratic republic through the monumental efforts, endeavors, struggles, and sacrifices of the common Nepali people. Through this, we must establish lasting peace in the country, strengthen democracy and the democratic system of governance, collectively create a shared agenda for the country's journey of prosperity, and ensure that Nepal remains a free, independent, sovereign nation forever. This should be our direction and our roadmap. Based on this foundation, on this theoretical ground, I want to say a few things to the government in the assembly, I want to raise a few points. Please, I don't mind speaking openly, ministers are present. I am not a person who minds speaking. We won't go off track, Mr. Chairman, will we? The issue is, a new government has come, I don't want to go too far back, around August 23-24. A new government has come, it's a government of the youth, the Prime Minister himself is very young. The country has very high expectations from the government. The government has done its best to fulfill the promises it made to the people. There is a sufficient majority in the House of Representatives. Even if you are not present in the National Assembly, the National Assembly has played a constructive role. It has helped you. Even when some of your people were absent, the policy and program were passed here. The bills you brought have also been passed with minor amendments in a very short period. Our best wishes and hopes are that the government can do some good work for the people under this system. Whether you have taken this as a priority or not, I don't know. But one thing I will say is that this is a parliamentary system. Ministers are present in the cabinet, but the minutes are signed by the ministers. Whatever the Prime Minister wants, that is the decision. Even if a minister's proposal goes, it doesn't become a decision without the Prime Minister's desire. This is a parliamentary system. It is a parliamentary system, but the Prime Minister and ministers are accountable to parliament individually and collectively. This is not just a political arrangement, it is a constitutional arrangement. Whether the issue is raised in the National Assembly or the House of Representatives, whether questions are asked about the Prime Minister or the ministers, they must come on time and answer the questions raised in parliament. That is accountability, that is accountability to the people. Why is the government unable to fulfill that? Why is the Prime Minister unable to fulfill it? When the Prime Minister does not come to parliament to answer the questions raised in parliament and does not want to convey what he has addressed to the public through parliament, a serious suspicion arises, and it has arisen in the market, in the political market, in political circles, everywhere. It is not just personal, it has arisen everywhere. Why is it difficult for him to run the country from within the office of the Prime Minister? Why is it difficult for him to work openly, transparently, and accountably? He should be able to tell us that. We are ready to support him. But the style of governance from within the office pushes only towards a great disaster for democracy, the democratic system of governance, and the constitution. It goes beyond the arrangement and leads to it. Therefore, my appeal to the government is that the Prime Minister and ministers should be fully accountable to parliament and answer the questions raised there. These are questions to the public. Questions raised in parliament are questions from the public. If a wrong question is raised, a question with a wrong intention, you can answer it and refute the question, you can establish your position. If a correct question is raised as a suggestion, you can accept it. That gives you strength, it gives you strength. When you express your views, you appear credible to the public. If you have done something wrong, accepting the questions raised here as suggestions will help you. Why are you not doing this? When I spoke before, I didn't speak this much, I just said I would cooperate fully. All of us here, to you, to the government. This is our advice, and it is also the reality. There is no representation of the ruling party here now, what is our role? Our role should be constructive, this is our advice. Why are you not paying attention to this, the questions raised there? Let this receive your serious attention. Why are you not answering? Mr. Chairman, I want to draw the special attention of the Prime Minister. This system is one where the Prime Minister is accountable to parliament, and he must fulfill it, otherwise the fundamental spirit of the constitution will be undermined. The fundamental spirit will be undermined, the foundation will crumble. The direction of action will crumble, be obstructed, and obstacles will arise, and various suspicions will arise, and various conflicts will arise, and from within those conflicts, those who do not want this system, those who do not want democracy, those who do not want the democratic system of governance, can cause incidents by infiltrating in many ways. Therefore, the government should be aware of this, this is my suggestion to the government. Another thing, I want to tell the government, there are currently three tiers of government: local, provincial, and federal. We have not yet been able to establish the provincial governments as governments. This is the reality. Provincial governments do not have police, and without police, they cannot maintain law and order. The schedules of the constitution state that there will be a police organization within the province, and the provincial government has the responsibility to maintain peace and order within the province. However, provincial governments have not been established in that manner yet. But I have a word, an appeal to the government: after these three tiers of government are in place, in the incident in Sunsari, in the incident in Siraha, how many times have you and the government officials, the concerned ministers, or bureaucrats, secretaries, met with the Chief Ministers of the provinces? How much coordination have you done with the people of the provincial government? How many times have you met with the ministers there? How much support have you sought from the heads of local governments to resolve all this? How many times have you met them? It won't work by just giving orders and directives from the center; solutions must be found. Where is the conspiracy, where is the conspiracy, or is this incident accidental, or is there a grand design behind it that will destroy many things? Is this the beginning of a conspiracy, or is it just an accidental event? Why is the federal government itself not taking this seriously? If it could be understood only through the security agencies at the center and in the provinces, this incident would not have happened. Therefore, in the coming days, the government must play its role in maintaining peace and order by coordinating with provincial and local governments. As the constitution provides from time to time, you must call the Chief Ministers for meetings, listen to them, take their suggestions, and you must also tell the provincial governments what you need from them. That was not seen this time. Such a major incident has occurred, nationwide, but your role was not seen at all. Neither coordination with the Chief Minister of Madhesh was seen, nor coordination with the Chief Minister of Koshi Province. This way, it won't work. The government is of the people, the government is not responsible to any particular party. This current government, Prime Minister Deuba, is not just the Prime Minister of Rastriya Swatantra Party, he is the Prime Minister of all Nepali people. We should look at it that way. If you have that perspective, and if you remain with the attitude that 'my party is not there at the local level, my party is not there,' how can you fulfill your role and lead society forward? Therefore, I appeal that your attention be drawn to this. I say to the government, why has the government not called the political parties when such an incident occurred? Why did the Prime Minister himself not call them? Why did the Prime Minister not call your own party, Rastriya Swatantra Party, the opposition parties, and the small parties, not only the parties represented in parliament but also the parties outside, and especially the political parties active in Koshi and Madhesh, and discuss with them in a timely manner?

And... I still feel that if it hadn't happened, I still feel that the incidents in Sunsari have increased and perhaps this is what I feel. You have failed in that this time. Therefore, it is not that such incidents will not happen again in the coming days. Anything can happen. Therefore, in the coming days, you must be able to take all political parties into confidence. Look, one cannot reach anywhere alone. This is a multi-party system. It has some definite values and principles. It has some norms, some principles. I have read and learned. A minister said yesterday that there was a generation gap, or something like that, with Krishna Dai, he told me. Okay, fine, I accept it. Whether it's my generation gap or yours, understand this incident. In this incident, put your hand on your chest and find the answer yourself from within. You don't need to tell us, speak here with the answer that comes from you, speak here. We have a time limit for how many hours you speak, you speak for as many hours as you want, speak. What are you doing? What do you want? What do you want from us? How do you want to save, protect, and uplift the public through us? Tell us. We are ready to help. That was not seen this time. I suggest to you that such a thing does not happen again in the future. The Prime Minister addressed, but did not dialogue with the public. This is the place for dialogue with the public. The questions raised here are the public's questions, you answer them, then there will be dialogue with the public. Answer the questions raised in the House of Representatives here, then there will be dialogue with the public. Two-way dialogue happens from there. Therefore, just addressing is not enough. You did well, it's good that you did, I don't say it's bad, but present your views here, come to the House of Representatives, come to the National Assembly, you are listening very seriously, truly. Please convey this to the Prime Minister, honorable minister. Create a situation where you can speak here. Otherwise, how will you be able to encompass the views of all these political parties and civil society? Without saying much else, I will not say much about the activeness of the security bodies. I have seen the incident of August 23-24 well. My house was also burnt down, it was looted. The entire country was burnt. What loss would have happened to a citizen like me by burning, how much would have happened? Some people say, it's fine. But the government at that time was also not aware that such a thing would happen on the 23rd-24th. If they had known, perhaps it would not have happened. Honorable Members, I request that the condolence motion be passed unanimously. Honorable Members, the condolence motion has been passed unanimously. Honorable Members, now let us observe one minute of silence to express sorrow on the demise of former Constituent Assembly Member, former House of Representatives Member, and former Deputy Prime Minister Gopal Man Shrestha. (Silence observed) Thank you. The next meeting of the National Assembly will be held on Saturday, August 3, 2083 (BS). Honorable Members, this meeting is adjourned until Saturday, August 3, 2083 (BS), Monday, at 1:15 PM. (Thereafter, the next meeting of the National Assembly was adjourned until Saturday, August 3, 2083 (BS), Monday, at 1:15 PM.) Adjourned: 15:54 hrs.

He condemns the government's perceived weakness and disappointment of the public. Honorable Member Rajendra Laxmi Gaire condemns the sowing of seeds of conflict and criticizes the government's approach to stability.
